initial_inventory.title: sm70: Defer QPN4 scratch for eager profiled engines

metadata.title: sm70: Defer QPN4 scratch for eager profiled engines
metadata.body:
## Purpose

While fitting Qwen3.8-27B's full 262K context onto two 16 GB V100s, I found 255 MiB per card tied up in persistent QPN4 prefill scratch.

Qualified QPN4 layers use temporary dense scratch automatically for eager engines with normally profiled KV memory. Graph-enabled engines and engines with a fixed KV byte budget keep resident scratch. `qpn4_lazy_dense_workspace` defaults to automatic; `true` forces temporary scratch and `false` forces resident scratch.

Temporary scratch is allocated inside the native M>1 prefill operation. M=1 decode uses no dense scratch. Availability is checked before weight conversion; the existing TurboMind fallback remains available if admission fails. This is an availability check, not a reservation against later fragmentation.

## Test Plan

Run `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_sm70_nvfp4_small_prefill.py` on SM70 and `pytest tests/quantization/test_sm70_nvfp4_kernel_selection.py`. Compare after-load allocation and branch-default throughput.

## Acceleration and benchmark contract

- Default enabled or opt-in: automatic for eager engines with normal KV profiling; resident scratch for graph-enabled engines and fixed KV budgets.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: `--kernel-config '{"sm70_nvfp4":{"qpn4_lazy_dense_workspace":true}}'`; `false` forces resident scratch. No environment switch was added.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: `fp8_e4m3`.
- Wheel SHA or source commit: source commit `9efdccd89`; no wheel.
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries: benchmark-only `upstream_probe_worker.ProbeWorker` on PYTHONPATH; native extensions reused from the pinned baseline build.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: the server selected `Qpn4NvFp4LinearKernel` and logged the M=1 decode path; captured greedy text matched at 30K and 120K.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: QPN4 qualification and TurboMind fallback are unchanged.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: new `qpn4_lazy_dense_workspace` field uses `null` for automatic policy; no environment alias was added.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: no environment variable changed; generated reference check passed.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no new environment variable; applies only to existing qualified QPN4 layers.

## Test Result

After-load allocated memory, per card:

| Workspace policy | Allocated bytes |
|---|---:|
| Resident | 10,129,392,128 |
| Lazy | 9,862,005,248 |

Lazy allocation saves 255 MiB of persistent storage per card; prefill still allocates temporary dense scratch.

Throughput: Qwen3.8-27B QUASAR NVFP4, TP2, dual V100 at 200 W/card; 30,063 cold prompt tokens, 128 generated tokens, three samples per state, prefix caching off. No sampled thermal-slowdown flags:

| State | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Pinned upstream, before | 1587.6 | 17.31 |
| Branch default | 1586.2 | 17.02 |
| Pinned upstream, after | 1586.9 | 17.06 |

The native suite passed 121 SM70 numerical, graph-replay and admission/fallback cases, plus 34 kernel-selection and engine-policy cases. The generated environment reference check passed after rebase.
